topic: How AI agents cut enterprise support costs

slides.hook: How **AI agents cut enterprise support costs**

slides.title: Deflect low‑value tickets at source
slides.body: Agents handle repetitive queries before they hit your team—passwords, status checks, basic troubleshooting—cutting ticket volume by 25–40% within one quarter.

slides.title: Shorter handle time, same headcount
slides.body: Agents draft replies, surface knowledge articles and propose next actions in‑tool. Agents prepare, humans approve—driving 20–35% faster resolution without new hires.

slides.title: First‑contact resolution goes up
slides.body: Context‑aware agents see history, contracts and config in one view. They guide agents to the right fix first time, reducing escalations by 15–25% and rework costs.

slides.title: Knowledge stays current, automatically
slides.body: Support agents waste time hunting outdated answers. AI agents propose article updates after every interaction, trimming time‑to‑answer and cutting training overhead.

slides.title: Shifts from firefighting to prevention
slides.body: Analytic agents scan ticket trends, flag root causes and estimate cost per pattern. Ops teams fix upstream issues that drive thousands of avoidable contacts a month.

slides.title: Measured savings, not vague promises
slides.body: Track deflection rate, cost per ticket, average handle time and FCR by channel. Tie agent performance to £ per contact and redeployed FTE, not ‘AI activity’.

slides.title: Governed agents fit regulated support
slides.body: Guardrails enforce policy: approved templates, PII redaction, audit logs and route‑to‑human rules for high‑risk cases. Cost savings without compliance surprises.

slides.line: Ready to quantify your support cost reduction?

caption:
AI agents are already taking 30–40% of support load in large enterprises.

The value is not chatbots for their own sake.
It is measurable savings in cost per contact, headcount plans and service quality.
The difference comes from design, adoption and governance.
